where: crates/blaze-kernel/src/session.rs (`Session::asked`), the carry loop in blaze-kernel's nest (`carry`), crates/blaze-cargo/src/serve/front_carry.rs
what: A carry repairs a reached row in place only when another step read it (`Session::asked` gives its key); a root that no step reads (front-items' `lines(file)`, `modules(crate)` in the daemon) is dropped and counted `gone`, even when its value would be equal. That is said only in `asked`'s one-line doc. The lane predicted every reached root repaired, five of six pinned counts were wrong, and the driver silently lost an edited file's `lines` until it asked them again.
cost: one compile-and-test round trip with the main agent
cause: the kernel compares a repaired row's value under the key its readers name it by; a root has no such key, so the carry has nothing to compare it under
class: a semantic of a core API stated only where it is implemented, not on the entry point callers read (`Kernel::carry`, `Carried::gone`)
prevention: `Kernel::carry`'s and `Carried::gone`'s docs say a reached root with no reader is dropped and must be asked again
workaround: the driver asks each edited file's `items` and `lines` again after the carry (`Built::ran` counts the reruns)
fix: none yet: a doc line on `Kernel::carry`, or the kernel repairing readerless roots under their own key
